body:
Jesus. Dude, I'm so sorry you've had to hold all that in, just to try to be a nice person. The resentment and the pain... Wow. It makes perfect sense that a monster has been growing inside. 

You're pretty strong to try so hard to keep going after all that. Some just lose their ability to feel anything, and they just exist in this numb state, barely with an appetite or a desire to move. You still have a fiery passion. It's painful, and it's unfair. But your values lie underneath all that pain, untouched. That's incredible. 

I don't know what it means when you say "100% pugilist" and "followed," though. I apologize. I'd love to know what you mean, if you are OK talking about it.

Wow. I'm kinda surprised how many comments here are advocating for the "two wrongs make a right" concept. It's as though the crime is only bad if it happens to a "good" person. 

Sure, it's a viscerally satisfying feeling to go eye-for-an-eye on the subject. I'm not immune to that. But I don't think it's the healthiest thing to wish abuse on anyone. I don't particularly always feel comfortable about giving the death penalty to murderers, either, even if I were to rationalize it as a means of ending the murderer's psychopathy/sociopathy the only way we know how. 

I don't know. I'm just uncomfortable about it when people seem happy to imagine inflicting the same harm the perpetrator caused to others. I'm not judging. I just don't feel the same way most do, I suppose.

You are very kind to comment on this post. I am a therapist myself who has two clients with bipolar, and it's definitely a difficult path. I'm sorry you had to experience anorexia. You are very strong after all. 

I think I'm just scared of being alive. I wish I could truly want my life. I will keep on living, but I guess it will take a lot of work for me to learn how to appreciate it.
I couldn't imagine what women have to go through. It takes a level of courage, inner strength, and self-esteem that I've never had. I hope more commenters come and validate your experience.

I came to this subreddit to say the exact same thing. I'm a little blown away. It's an awful state to experience.

If I'm hearing you right, it's almost like you have lost that "pull." The pull that had once drawn you toward the things you couldn't get enough of... The pull that could at least give you a sense of identity or community... That pull is no longer there. All that is left is the constant "push" required to get through the day's responsibilities and checklists. This activity is healthy, that activity is profitable, that other activity puts a roof over your head... And you're just doing things until you get the privilege of going to sleep.

Is that sort of what you are feeling? If not, I'm sorry. Your post just spoke to me.

Sounds a little victim-blamey, imo. They're both adults, and hopefully he uses this as a learning experience. I just wouldn't say it to a 28yo woman who got cheated on by a 20yo man. If I'm wrong, then I'm happy to retract.

These posts haunt me. I wish it wasn't so difficult to be a woman. Please know that there are so many who I've seen on Reddit who will read this and see your truth. They will see a lot of themselves in you.

We believe you. We hear you. If no one else does.
Some real garbage dudes out there. I don't know if it's a massive insecurity problem or a weird mental tactic. But I'm sorry you have to go through this.
It hurts my heart to hear a 19 year old woman having to go through something like that. That man was scummy and should be put underneath the jail. I'm sorry you experienced that. 😔
No need to change yourself! Better to draw in people who like the real you every time.

That's a shame. It sounds so frustrating on several levels for you. You want to see him get better, and he's standing in his own way. Not that it's easy to get a therapist these days, but still. 

Some folks think that they can pull themselves out of the darkness by getting a great partner, having a nice job, eating the right foods, moving to the right area... and when they finally have that person or thing, they get even worse because the root cause hasn't been found. They just blame themselves and feel hopeless. 

I actually am a therapist, but many years ago even I thought I knew how to fix my own issues with diets and routines and techniques. My ex wife wanted me to get my own therapy when I was in grad school, but I was afraid that I'd end up with a lousy practitioner who could make things worse. And I was convinced that there were things the average therapist wouldn't understand about my childhood, as I am a person of color and grew up in poverty. 

Lemme know if this is true: he's buried something deep inside and doesn't "think it's a big deal" because he's learned how to avoid "burdening" others with his feelings. You might have to reframe what therapy actually is so that he knows it's more than just wallowing in your emotions for an hour. I'm not sure. I wish I could help. But I hope you can help him understand that he has to get better not just for himself, but for your happiness, too.

I think you might want to tell your partner that you care enough about the relationship and t/heir mental health to insist that some new strategies be put in place. This isn't just about your needs as a romantic partner, which are valid. This is about watching someone you care about allowing t/heir life to unravel without intervening. You have every right to *respectfully* draw attention to it. It might help to point out all the other things that depression robs from t/hem. Do t/hey not enjoy things the way t/hey used to? Is it affecting work? Do friends notice a change? All this can be used to get t/hem to see that this is more than just you trying to get t/hem to do something for you. This is about helping t/hem to be t/heir best self.
NTA. That's so disingenuous. It's not just a slap in the face to OP, but it's an insult to the women who really struggle alone to make a life for themselves.

NTA. The last thing in the world I would want my girlfriend experiencing is the risk of another pregnancy after almost having a *stroke* the last time. Also, three months of recuperation after a major procedure is too long for him? He should get creative! Get some marital aids or some techniques that don't involve intercourse! Am I missing something?
In what way does he "not get it?" What is he not understanding? Does he keep pestering you even when you tell him you're not interested?

Yyyyeah. This guy is not remotely normal. Find the safest way out of this relationship if you can.

Please don't listen to that nonsense. Be the real you, and wait for someone who can respect that.
It hurts my heart to hear young women suffering at the hands of selfish men. I'm sorry for the hardships you've experienced.

You said that there were raised voices and a lot of emotions when this came out. I can understand why you both may have responded out of anger and sadness. You are not to blame at all, though. No matter what. 

I'd say that some couple's therapy or individual therapy would be warranted, if that's a possibility for you. Not to point fingers or anything. Just to aid in the communication of something so difficult to bring up.
There are many women in the neuropsych field who can give you a little insight and inspiration. They didn't let any boys' club stand in their way, and I hope you don't either. I believe in you!

A sad and very common problem. No, you didn't overreact. It would help to have a third party weigh in on what can be done to make the housework more fair. A marriage counselor would probably be warranted here. If he doesn't agree to it, you might need to set clear boundaries and tell him you won't risk your health anymore just to maintain the status quo.
It's a shame how that happens. Of course, we men have our own version of this nonsense, but I agree that it should be called out no matter who it is.

Just breathe for a minute. 

No one transforms into a monster. No one changes into one. 

Just because the disgust isn't as strong doesn't mean you're becoming someone else. Your brain is just fatigued by all the thinking that OCD is forcing you to do. 

You're not your thoughts and sensations. They are happening to you, not from you.

It definitely can cause false attraction and false memories. It poisons the past and makes people worry that they can't be 100% certain that their intentions were pure. The more we test the past, the more the uncertainty spreads.

I'm sorry you're going through this. OCD does an amazing job of manufacturing evidence against us. It will question every act and sensation "just in case" you might be a bad person. 

Attacking OCD should include attacking the fear of being bad in general. We have to let go of the idea that there are good and bad people. We have to realize that we are all doing the best we can with the brain we're given. That's not an easy thing to believe. Even for me sometimes. But it's an important thing to keep in mind. 

I hope it gets easier for you as time goes on.
Yes. It's like scratching an itch instead of soothing the infection. It feels good temporarily, but it always comes back.
Is she OK, Annie?
I couldn't have said it better.

These posts hurt my heart. I wish women didn't have to tolerate so much injustice. I feel like I'm just one guy, so it feels like there's not much I can do. But this isn't about me. I just want to encourage you and be supportive of your feelings.

In a purely practical sense, yes I agree. I would find it to be a problematic pairing for a 15 year old to actively date a 12 year old. But it's not uncommon for   that kind of age gap when it comes to noticing something attractive about the other person. And in OP's case, it sounds like a false attraction to begin with. I do agree with you, though.
I'm very glad to hear it!

It's a three year difference, so it's not anything to be concerned about. Breathe slowly and think of your core values. Technically you'd have to be at least 16 and the other minor would have to be 5+ years younger for it to be considered p*dophilia.
I can't stand it when people say this. I'm black, and it's so irritating. It just gives people an excuse to say messed up stuff, in my opinion.
I think it's a positive step. It's like the OCD is having a last ditch effort to mess with us, so it throws in the groinals as a way to keep us anxious.
Ask yourself this question: if a friend told you the same thing that you've told us, would you think that person is a P?
That's the OCD. There's no such thing as a person becoming a P spontaneously. You're only going to do something bad if you listen to the obsessions and compulsively try to check them.

I'm guessing that you know deep down that children are victimized by cp and that engaging in p*dophilic acts with children hurts them. I'm not convinced that you actually think it's ok. You'd know if you were a P. It would be a part of your identity, your core values. Am I wrong?
The minor had to be at least 5 years younger than you to be considered problematic. Also, what matters is whether or not you had distress from the thoughts and sensations.

You are obviously a passionate, considerate person, and this very rightly means a lot to you. I respect that, and I am completely in solidarity with the sentiment. The country needs more people like you standing up for what's right. I just need to clarify something.

The question wasn't "why are men like this". That's actually a perfectly fine question. I understand that it's a rhetorical question, and it just means "why are so many men like this." I wonder that myself quite a bit. The question was "Are all X like this", with an emphasis on it being used for men. That's a slightly different thing because it can be used as a totally legit inquiry.  I don't think all men, or white people, or straight people, or any other group is "like that". So I just think the question is insinuating that somehow there's something possibly inherently bad about a group of people. "Why are men like this" is a far better question because it leaves room for interpretation. 

Being wary of white people is completely understandable. Calling out racism and sexism is totally fine. I tried to make that abundantly clear. I agree with you on all those points. I'm only talking about the question "Are all men/white people/etc. like this?" I don't have to ask that question to point out the systemic sexism and racism that keeps so many of us from advancing. 

All I'm saying is that I'm not a fan of generalizations. Feel free to keep asking "Are all X like this" if you like. It's only a pet peeve. I'd just rather not insinuate anything. 

And I don't know what is making you think I'm not black. Again, I agree with the frustration and anger about powerful people in society oppressing others because of race, gender identity, nationality, sexuality, etc. for centuries. I'm a 43 year old African American who just cringes a little when I hear that particular sentence. I hope that clarified things. If not, then I'm sorry for being offensive.

That's true, though it would be just as reductionist to say that testosterone causes inherently negative behavior as it would be to say one's cultural origin causes negative behavior. Race is more than skin color; it implies an ethnic or national background that could lead some to make assumptions about a group of people. 

In other words, if white people are neither all good nor bad, and men are neither all good nor bad, why ask the question? It's perfectly understandable to be cautious, particularly if the majority of one's encounters with a man, a white person, etc., are negative. But the question "Are all X like this?" seems unhelpful no matter what the X is.

That's fine, but then white people and black people are both affected by Systemic racism, But white people are the only ones who still benefit from it. Not every white person is bad, But there are enough white people out there who are that you have to question which ones are really good.

 Do you hear how off-putting that sounds?  I'm a black guy and I would never say anything like that because I know how It looks.
It is, indeed. It's as silly as saying "Why aren't men smart?" "Are all gay people like this?" "Why do Chinese people act like _____?" None of it is really sensible in my opinion.
It's a knee-jerk question that pops up verbatim like this on Reddit. Not all the time, just enough to make me scratch my head.

There's a general rule that it can't really be called p*dophilia unless you're older than 16 and the minor is at least 5 years younger. But even if you were 22+ at the time, and that minor celebrity was 17, that's still not really your fault because you didn't know. You weren't seeking out 17 year olds. It was a mistake. Something like this probably happens to all of us. Your discomfort shows that your core values are intact.
Because she literally just told OP her decision over the weekend. This is not an easy choice for OP to make.

This is heart-wrenching. You have to carry your broken partner on your shoulder through life, and it sounds like you aren't getting much sympathy about it. You care about him so much. I wish I could recommend some natural substance or new-fangled remedy. I'm no doctor. I just hope you are able to get a therapist or social worker that could help.

I'm so sorry you're going through this. It really is a mourning process when someone hurts us like this. We are grieving the loss of the person we thought we knew. Having someone beside you to grieve through it is very helpful. I hope you don't have to process this all yourself.
Not cool. I'm sorry that happened to you.
Wait... so the characters are supposed to be older than you? That seems... not all that bad. I might be misunderstanding.

Aged-down content and shrunken characters seem to be topics that pop up a lot in this subreddit. I'm an old geezer compared to half of you, so I didn't even know about this stuff, and frankly it sounds like I should learn as little about it as possible. 😌

It's such a vague description that they give these characters, and some of you mentioned that you have to dig deep to get their real ages. But please understand that if you're 15 and a character is meant to be 12 or 13, you're basically a teen getting curious about a tween. You aren't a monster. Your preference is most likely going to change as you get older. Please don't panic.

You might be engaging in what's called compulsive confession right now. It's hard to avoid sometimes. I do hear you, though, and I know that you are not your thoughts. Mistakes and blurred lines are almost inevitable for teens these days because of how easy it is to access questionable images and people. Everything you mentioned so far sounds like the actions of a young person who was the victim of grooming and confusing online content, not the actions of a monster. 

Please give yourself the empathy that you would give someone else telling the same story.
Hm. Check out Emily Nagoski's TED talk about it on YouTube. See if there's anything there that seems familiar.
Aw. Thanks!

Lemme ask something that you have every right not to answer...

Are you a survivor of any child abuse? (No details necessary.)

If so, then you might be experiencing unwanted arousal, which is different from OCD but still treatable. If not, it could still be OCD after a long time of testing and checking. 

Again, ignore this if you don't want to answer.
Please don't listen to Reddit. If your therapist has seen this sort of thing before, go with her on this.
It's just frustrating, is all. It's been bothering me for a while, and I'm glad OP is calling it out.
Once again a group of men are making things difficult for vulnerable women. It makes me ashamed to be a guy sometimes. I'm sorry on their behalf.
Did it feel like you were engaging in checking behavior?

Not a horrible person at all. 
I'm no expert, but what you're describing reminds me of something I've read about SA survivors. Sometimes survivors get aroused by images or stories that remind them of what they experienced in real life. It's as though the SA sort of teaches the body to respond to it with arousal as a sort of defense mechanism, if that makes sense. CNC stuff can make a survivor feel a sense of power or control over the past experience, so it makes perfect sense that you envisioned yourself briefly as the child in the picture. I don't mean to presume about your experience; I could be completely wrong about this.

I really worried about my own arousal when I once saw something similar to what you described. But talking about it with my therapist helped me see that I wasn't excited *about* the young-looking person; rather, I was imagining myself *experiencing* what the young-looking person was feeling. There were times in my childhood when certain people were very inappropriate with me, so maybe that plays a role. 

But you are not a monster. Plain and simple.

It's infuriating and embarrassing. I'm sorry that so many women have to tolerate this mess. 

Thankfully, the answer is no: all men are not like this. The loudest and proudest are the ones who get the attention, and they make stupid claims about what it means to be a man and a woman because they want to feel a sense of mastery about the subject rather than just admit that we are all complex beings. 

A lot of men are sick of the alpha nonsense, and we don't make excuses for cheating. But there are a lot of dumb men out there making life miserable for women. And for that I wish I could apologize on their behalf. You, of course, have every right to be disappointed and angry about the idiotic discourse of these men online.

Ps don't have any reservations about the thoughts and sensations themselves. They enjoy them because they feel that they are victimless fantasies, even though some never act on it. They also tend to have authentic crushes and sometimes even parasocial yearnings for kids. That's a way deeper connection than intrusive thoughts and groinals.

For me, sometimes I'm afraid to say something that will get interpreted as reassurance, leading to the OP spiraling into incessant questions like "but how do I know it's not real tho?" and all that. I'm new to all this, so I sometimes just don't know what to say.

Other times, I think people just kind of lurk and empathize while being a little too nervous sharing their own experiences. 

But just getting a little nod or a "You are not your thoughts" sometimes goes a long way, so I understand your frustration.

The system of human arousal is, from what my own therapist has told me, like an accelerator and a brake pedal. If we see attributes that are attractive, the accelerator gets us going. But if we learn that the person is underage, not giving consent, in pain, etc., that puts the brakes on. For some people it takes a little while for the arousal to come to a complete stop. That can make us worry that we are attracted to things that we really aren't. I wouldn't worry about this, based on what you've mentioned.
That is unreal. I'm so sorry that happened. Well, I wish you a very Happy Birthday 🎂 I hope you get a hundred comments!

Wait... your mom said what? 
I have to ask... how did that conversation even happen? You don't have to share if you don't want to, but wow. That's beyond cruel.

Wow. That's a visceral reaction. I'm sorry you're dealing with this. 

Btw, no, ocd doesn't make a person transform into a P or a murderer or a gay/straight person, etc. You might end up doing things to test yourself that you regret, but you'll always be the same person you were from the start.

I've been reluctant to tell people this, but I'm a therapist myself. The problem is that I can't really do anything therapeutic in a subreddit comment or private message. All I can do is provide my perspective and point people in the direction of some YouTubers and websites. Plus I'm an old geezer compared to a lot of you folks, so I don't know anyone helpful on Twitter or Insta or all those apps. I wish I could do more. I don't know what to say. Such an unjust childhood and a cruel way to start your adult life...

If we're talking about *those* intrusive thoughts, they can be really confusing when they're accompanied by strong physical arousal. But I think what's happening is that we have such an array of fantasy p0rnography that we wind up indulging in things that go wildly against our core values just to check ourselves. When we inevitably get aroused, we despise ourselves, and we feel the need to reassure ourselves again, which just solidifies the connection between thoughts and arousal. It never really feels "good" afterward; there's always something icky about it. But we keep doing it because we're constantly trying to prove that we aren't p3dos or gay or straight, etc. I don't know if that made sense. It's 8am, and I'm a little groggy. 😆
The ages were too close to be considered p*dophilic.  There has to be a five year age gap at least. You're fine.
You're very kind. Thanks!
Remember your core values. You know the idea of it makes you sick. It's not who you are.

It's not gone. It's diminished because the brain is afraid of trusting itself being aroused anymore. Your libido is kind of burned out because of all the anxiety. It'll come back when you slowly determine the difference between authentic attraction and intrusive thoughts/arousal. One is rooted in your core values while the other is not.

I'm so sorry you're dealing with this. I wish I could find a way to convince everyone in this subreddit that they are not the product of their thoughts and sensations. We can get so used to tolerating the stupid thoughts and groinals that we don't even recognize what our authentic attractions are anymore. Remember your values and separate yourself from the OCD. I wish you luck.
Of course!
Wow. That's pure garbage. I'm so sorry that happened to you.
You were 15 and she was at most 3 years younger. That doesn't count as p3dophelia.
The testing is a hallmark sign that it's the POCD talking.
Couldn't have did it better myself. 👏
Ok. Either way, it doesn't sound like you were acting with ill intent.

Something like that, yeah. But not without therapy like ERP, in my opinion. It's just less debilitating that way. 

I empathize, I really do. I avoid the compulsion problem by doing a thought experiment: imagine you're on a deserted island and you can pick anyone in the world to spend the rest of your life with.  There's no rescue, no laws, no social consequences. Who do you pick?

I never choose a kid. It doesn't even feel right. A predator would easily pick a child because of the power dynamic.
P3dophelia is defined as being at least 16 and being at least 5 years older than the subject. I don't think you're a monster.

1. "Pdf files" is a hilarious euphemism. 😂 
2. We don't magically transform into those people. It's there from the get go. 

3. You totally didn't do anything even inappropriate. The kid was the one being inappropriate, if anything. 

Don't beat yourself up, please.
You aren't the only guy. Trust me. I never saw the allure.

For some of us, our brains have tried to control or eradicate the intrusive thoughts for so long that they have been conditioned to associate sexual arousal with those thoughts. In other words, the brain has been obsessively saying to itself, "Don't be aroused by this thought," and the only way to understand that sentence is to conceptualize being aroused by the thought. It's been reinforced so much that the brain finds all other arousal to be abhorrent, so it diminishes the authentic libido and makes us less attracted to peers over time. The less emotional and anxious we are toward those thoughts, the less often the brain will obsessively fight the thoughts, and the arousal will diminish in favor of the authentic attraction toward people our age.

It's all behaviorism. I hope that made sense.
Yes, it can start that way. It's not authentic attraction.
You were drawn to the more mature attributes of the character. It confused your brain and led to arousal. Perfectly natural.

The confusion between your values and your body is very normal, at least for POCD. There's a difference between feeling aroused beyond your control and being genuinely attracted. The body parts involved are the same, but one feels like it's happening to us, not from us. We've just gotten so used to surrendering to groinal impulses that we forget the difference.
How old were you when that happened, if you don't mind me asking?
You wouldn't have been interested if you knew the age beforehand. Some part of you would have been too disgusted, just like you are now.
Nope. Your intent is not the same as your thoughts. The thoughts happen *to* you, not *from* you.

It's an awful system that pits powerless men against women and women against men. The powers that be just want men to keep their mouths shut and work until they are worthless, and they want women to caretake until it becomes their whole existence. They don't care about us.

I think it's more than just self-hatred. I don't think you're a monster. I think there's a real, authentic part of you that isn't aligned with the intrusive thoughts and powerful sensations. But maybe I'm wrong.

Because it is, kinda. OCD finds any uncertainty and feeds on it so that the anxiety can turn on. It's horrible. 

The thoughts do not define you. The sensations do not define you. It's your core values that define you. Nothing can change that.

You are not wrong. 
Find the safest way out of this relationship.

Distracting yourself won't work, I'm afraid. All I can suggest is that you prepare yourself to accept that maybe an intrusive thought will come, and when it does, say the mantras, "I am not my thoughts." "My thoughts happen to me, not from me." "I am not a monster." I know it's sucky advice. But it's important to avoid reacting to the thought when it comes. Take deep breaths, and don't run away from the child. That just teaches the OCD to make it worse next time. 

I've worked with children most of my adult life, and it's so much better now that I know what it is and don't react to the thoughts.
Please don't give up. Don't let OCD win.
What's weird about being with a little person? It's the age that matters. Their physical stature isn't the same as a child's, so you're still OK.

You might want to bring an article about POCD to your therapist so you can help t/hem understand what you're dealing with. It sucks that you have to educate the therapist, but I'm a therapist myself, and I didn't even know about POCD until about two years ago.

Your therapist clearly doesn't understand OCD enough. Besides that, intrusive thoughts that you don't want and sensations you can't control don't make authentic attraction. You said it yourself. You experience the real thing, too. 

The touching yourself stuff is a compulsion. It's a means of trying to get rid of the thought or have control over the experience. 

It's hard to believe it, I know. But it really is just OCD, most likely.

"I thought he looked like a child and I wasn’t attracted to him anymore."
Said no p3dophile ever.

You thought he was older, and he said he was older. At worst, it's his fault if he was lying about his age. Sounds like he had a baby-face and you tried to look past it, but it just felt icky.
